title: Recording Fiddler on the Roof on short notice
summary: The record company drops the Fiddler on the Roof score, rehearsed at Pep's in Philadelphia, but the album sold only modestly.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Yeah, and so finally uh, the record companies would always come and drop a score on the band, you know.

Say we want you to record this one. So uh, when Charles was in the band we was playing at the Pep's Bar in Philadelphia. Fiddler on the Roof, they wanted us to record, the music for Fiddler on the Roof. And the guy who wrote the music, they sent the guy down there with the score, a guy come into Philadelphia and so Cannon say we have a rehearsal tomorrow at Pep's Bar at 2:00 and we're gonna rehearse it then. The guy was gonna come with the score. Bamm, drop the score, and we gotta make an album, Fiddler on the Roof, so we got it. So everybody put their heads together and we made the album and you heard the album, it was a very good album.
But it didn't, it didn't, the record didn't
sell too good, too much it sold, but it didn't sell like they thought it was gonna sell.
